title: Protocol for structural and biochemical analyses of RhoA GTPase
protocol: Transform the expression plasmids into BL21(DE3) competent cells.
Plate the transformed samples to LB-Ampicillin plates.
Incubate at 37°C for 12–16 hours.
Inoculate a single colony into 5 mL LB media supplemented with 100 μg/mL Ampicillin.
Incubate at 37°C with shaking at 220 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.5.
Add 600 μL of cell culture to 400 μL autoclaved 80% glycerol in a 2 mL screw-cap tube.
Freeze the glycerol stock tube in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen glycerol stock at −80°C.
Inoculate with a gentle stubbing from the glycerol stock using a sterile pipette tip into 100 mL LB media supplemented with 100 μg/mL Ampicillin.
Incubate at 37°C with shaking at 220 rpm for 12–16 h.
Dilute the fully-grown culture 1:100 in 6× 1 L LB media supplemented with 100 μg/mL Ampicillin in 6× 2.8-L Fernbach culture flasks.
Incubate at 37°C with shaking at 220 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.6–0.8.
Add 0.2 mL 1 M IPTG to each flask to reach a final concentration of 0.2 mM.
Reduce the shaker temperature to 20°C, keep incubating with shaking for 12–16 h.
Add glycerol to re-suspended cells to ∼10% (v/v).
Flash freeze the mixture in liquid nitrogen and store at −80°C for up to 6 months.
Add PMSF to the re-suspended cells at a final concentration of 1 mM.
Add DTT to the re-suspended cells at a final concentration of 10 mM.
Sprinkle lysozyme over the re-suspended cells.
Lysate the cells by sonication on ice for 5 min at 60% power with intervals of 20 s on and 10 s off.
Spin down the cell lysate at 35,000 × g for 1 h at 4°C to remove debris and insoluble fractions.
Wash a 5 mL GSTrap FF column with at least 5 column volume (CV) Milli-Q water using a peristaltic pump at 5 mL/min.
Wash the GSTrap FF column with at least 5 CV GST buffer A using a peristaltic pump at 5 mL/min.
Load the supernatant of cell lysate to the equilibrated GSTrap FF column at 1 mL/min.
Wash the GSTrap FF column with at least 5 CV GST buffer A.
Wash the column with at least 2 CV Thrombin cleavage buffer.
Dissolve 10 mg thrombin in 2.5 mL Thrombin cleavage buffer and load it to the column.
Incubate the column at 25°C for 1 h or at 4°C for 12–16 h to cleave proteins.
Wash the column with 5 CV GST buffer A.
Collect the flow through from the column carefully, avoiding air bubbles.
Concentrate the flow through to a final volume of 2 mL using an Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Unit at 6,000 × g at 4°C.
Inject the concentrated sample onto HiLoad 16/600 Superdex 200 pg column pre-equilibrated with Gel filtration buffer and run at 1 mL/min.
Pool protein-containing fractions from the RhoA elution at ∼90 mL.
Concentrate the pooled protein to approximately 1 mL using Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Unit (10 KDa MWCO) at a speed of 6,000 × g at 4°C.
Measure the concentration using Bradford reagent.
Aliquot and store the sample in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage at -80°C.
Wash CIP-agarose beads with 20 mM Tris pH 7.5 for three times.
Add RhoA-GDP sample to washed CIP-agarose beads, along with GMPPNP or GTPγS at a concentration of 10 molar fold.
Bring the final volume to 1.5 mL using Nucleotide exchange buffer and rotate at 4°C for 12–16 hours.
Spin down the CIP-agarose beads by centrifuging at maximum speed for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Wash the beads with 0.5 mL of 20 mM Tris pH 7.5, spin down, and combine the wash with the supernatant.
Inject the sample onto HiLoad 16/600 Superdex 200 pg column pre-equilibrated with Gel filtration buffer and run at 1 mL/min.
Pool protein-containing fractions from the RhoA elution at ∼90 mL.
Concentrate the pooled protein to approximately 1 mL using Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Unit (10 KDa MWCO) at a speed of 6,000 × g at 4°C.
Measure the concentration using Bradford reagent.
Aliquot the sample.
Freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen.
Store the tubes at −80°C.
Add 10 mM EDTA and 5 mM GDP to the sample after step 16 for RhoA mutant G14V.
Let the protein sit at 25°C for 3 hours before proceeding to step 17.
Express GST-Rhotekin-RBD using steps 3–7 as above.
Purify GST-Rhotekin-RBD using steps 8–13 as above.
Elute the protein from the GSTrap column using GST elution buffer.
Concentrate the elution to 2 mL final volume using Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Unit at a speed of 6,000 × g at 4°C.
Inject the concentrated sample onto HiLoad 16/600 Superdex 200 pg column pre-equilibrated with Gel filtration buffer and run at 1 mL/min.
Pool protein-containing fractions.
Concentrate the protein to approximately 1 mL using Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Unit at a speed of 6,000 × g at 4°C.
Measure the concentration using Bradford reagent.
Aliquot the sample.
Freeze the aliquoted samples in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen samples at -80°C.
Add 50 μL of deuterium oxide to 450 μL of protein sample.
Transfer the mixed sample to 5 mm NMR tubes.
Record 1D 31P spectra at 275K and 298K on a Bruker Avance II 600 MHz spectrometer.
Insert the sample once the probe temperature is stable.
Allow the sample temperature to stabilize for 15 minutes minimum.
Adjust lock, tune and match on the 31P channel before starting data collection at each temperature.
Shim the sample before starting data collection at each temperature.

Acquire the data using 1D pulse program “zgpg30” from Bruker pulse library with time domain (TD) = 30k, DS = 8, spectral width (SW) = 100 ppm, acquisition time (AQ) = 0.6 s, relaxation delay (D1) = 3 s.
Adjust the number of scans (NS) depending on sample concentration.
Add increasing amounts of GST-Rhotekin-RBD to the NMR sample in molar ratios of 0.5, 1, and 2.
Incubate the samples at 25°C for 15 minutes after each addition of GST-Rhotekin-RBD.
Concentrate the samples back to 500 μL using an Amicon Ultra-0.5 Centrifugal Filter Unit (10 KDa MWCO) at a speed of 6,000 × g at 4°C.
Collect 31P spectra after each titration.
Process the spectra using Topspin 4.0 software (Bruker).
Manually phase and baseline correct all spectra.
Reference all spectra to phosphoric acid at 0.0 ppm.
Do not add extra GDP or GTP analogs to samples.
Collect spectra of free GDP and GTP analogs in the same buffer as controls.
Mix PEG/ion screen components for RhoA protein crystallization.
Generate diffracting crystals using hanging drop method with PEG/ion screen conditions.
Collect diffraction data from obtained crystals.
Determine structure of RhoA proteins in both GDP-bound and GMPPNP-bound states.
Concentration of RhoA proteins is around 8–10 mg/mL.
Mix 1 μL protein solution with 1 μL reservoir solution.
Equilibrate the mixture against 700 μL reservoir solution at 4°C using hanging drop vapor diffusion methods.
Grow RhoA crystals in 0.1 M Tris pH 8.3, 16%–20% PEG 8K, and 15% (v/v) 1,4-dioxane.
Observe plate crystal appearance in two days.
Reach maximum crystal size in 1–2 weeks.
Loop the crystals using appropriate size loops under the optical microscope.
Transfer the crystals with loops and wash them first in cryoprotect solution containing 0.1 M Tris pH 8.3, 15% (v/v) 1,4-dioxane, 25% (v/v) PEG 8K.
Wash the crystals again for several seconds in cryoprotect solution containing 0.1 M Tris pH 8.3, 15% (v/v) 1,4-dioxane, 30% (v/v) PEG 8K.
Loop the crystals again and freeze them mounted on loops in liquid nitrogen.
Ship the frozen crystals to Beamline 31D at the Advanced Photon Source (APS), Argonne National Laboratory.
Index and integrate the datasets using Mosflm.
Integrate the datasets using Scala.
Determine the structure of RhoAWT and RhoAG14V in complex with GDP by molecular replacement method using Phaser.
Use a searching model based on the structure of RhoA-GDP (PDB: 1FTN) for determining the structures of RhoAWT and RhoAG14V.
Determine the structure of RhoAWT in complex with GMPPNP using a searching model based on the structure of constitutively active RhoA (PDB: 1KMQ).
Refine the structures using Phenix.
Build models with Coot in alternative rounds.
Deposit final models and scaled reflection data to the PDB.
Add GDP or GMPPNP to crystallization samples after purification to a final concentration of 5 mM (∼10× of RhoA proteins).
Prepare the GST pull-down buffer.
Supplement the GST pull-down buffer with 10 μM GDP or appropriate GTP analogs.
Wash 10 μL GSH-agarose beads three times with 1 mL GST pull-down buffer.
Remove wash supernatant carefully to avoid losing any beads.
Add 20 μg of GST-Rhotekin-RBD protein to the washed beads.
Rotate the mixture at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Wash the beads three times with 1 mL GST pull-down buffer containing GDP or GTP analog.
Dilute RhoA samples to approximately 1 mg/mL using Bradford assay for quantification.
Add 5 μg of each RhoA sample to the beads in 100 μL GST pull-down buffer.
Rotate at 4°C for 1 hour with continuous rotation.
Wash the beads two times with 1 mL GST pull-down buffer containing GDP or GTP analog.
Add 20 μL 4× SDS Sample buffer.
Boil at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Load all the supernatant to a 15% SDS-PAGE gel.
Subject the gel to anti-RhoA Western Blot analysis using RhoA antibody diluted 1:2000.
Label GDP-bound or GMPPNP-bound RhoA proteins.
Titrate Rhotekin-RBD.
Compare Monolith systems to find the suitable one for the experiment.
Use Monolith NT.115 if multiple fluorescent channels are needed.
Choose Monolith NT.Labelfree if measuring interactions under native conditions is required.
Label one binding partner with NT-647 dye at cysteine residues for protein-protein interactions when using Monolith NT.115.
Ensure the concentration of the unlabeled partner is high enough to reach a final concentration at least 10-fold above the expected dissociation constant (KD).
Prepare labeled RhoA proteins using the Monolith Protein Labeling Kit RED-MALEIMIDE.
Exchange 100 μL of 20 μM RhoA protein sample into labeling buffer using column A.
Dissolve dye in 30 μL DMSO and vortex to mix well.
Dilute the dye to 2-3 fold of the protein concentration using labeling buffer.
Mix 100 μL of protein with 100 μL of diluted dye.
Incubate for 30 min at 25°C in the dark.
Remove extra dye using column B with MST sample storage buffer.
Calculate the concentration of the protein and dye using Nanodrop.
Measure absorption at 280 nm for protein and 650 nm for the dye.
Aliquot into PCR tubes, freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at -80°C.
Ensure you do not have too little or too much fluorescence intensity.
Check the labeling efficiency by comparing the fluorescence intensities of the labeled protein with free dye at the same concentration.
Adjust the concentration of the labeled molecule to achieve optimal fluorescence counts, ensuring it is between 200–1500 fluorescence counts.
Start the “capillary scan” with 50% LED power using a standard capillary.
Adjust sample concentration or vary LED power between 15% and 95% as needed for optimal fluorescence counts.
Choose the appropriate capillary type (standard, hydrophilic, or hydrophobic) that gives symmetrical fluorescence peaks.
Prepare the labeled molecules at the determined concentration in MST binding buffer.
Fill at least 4 capillaries with the prepared sample.
Perform the “Capillaries Scan” with the predetermined setting.
Measure the samples at 40% MST power.
Monitor for signs of aggregation during the measurement.
Optimize buffer if aggregation is observed.
Prepare 16 small micro reaction tubes and label them from 1 to 16.
Fill tube 1 with 20 μL of the highest concentration of the unlabeled molecule.
Fill tubes 2–16 with 10 μL of MST binding buffer each.
Transfer 10 μL from tube 1 to tube 2, mix very well by pipetting up and down several times.
Repeat the transfer and mixing steps for tubes 3 through 15 sequentially.
Remove 10 μL from tube 15 after mixing.
Tube 16 serves as the buffer control with MST binding buffer only.
Mix 10 μL of the fluorescent-labeled molecule at double the concentration with each titrated sample.
Incubate all samples and controls at 25°C for 30 minutes.
Fill the capillaries with prepared samples.
Measure the samples using 20%, 40%, and 80% MST power.
Start Affinity Analysis Software.
Load raw data.
Check the “Original Fluorescence” and ensure no concentration-dependent changes exceed 10%.
Troubleshoot by checking signal/noise ratio at different MST powers.
Use the lowest possible MST power for analysis with a good signal-to-noise ratio.
Select standard analysis mode as either “Thermophoresis” or “Thermophoresis with Jump”.
Determine KD using KD fit with default settings if multiple modes yield similar results.
Export data and load to GraphPad Prism for binding analysis if preferred.
Load BODIPY-FL-GDP to RhoA proteins.
Prepare 2 μM RhoA proteins and 1 μM BODIPY-FL-GDP in the BODIPY-FL-GDP loading buffer.
Add EDTA to a final concentration of 1 mM in the loading buffer.
Incubate the mixture at 25°C for 2 hours.
Terminate the exchange by adding 5 μL of 100 mM MgCl2 to each sample.
Prepare nucleotide dissociation assay buffer containing 5 mM MgCl2 and add 100 μL to each sample.
Aliquot 25 μL/well of BODIPY-FL-GDP loaded RhoA samples into a 384-well plate, with 6 wells total for each sample.
Prepare GMPPNP at concentrations of 2 μM, 5 μM, and 10 μM in the Nucleotide dissociation assay buffer.
Aliquot GMPPNP samples to a 96-well plate.
Prepare 1 μM RhoA-GDP proteins in the nucleotide association assay buffer, containing 5 mM MgCl2, with a total volume of 200 μL.
Aliquot 25 μL/well to a 384-well plate for each sample concentration.
Prepare 2 μM, 5 μM, and 10 μM BODIPY-FL-GTPγS in the nucleotide association assay buffer.
Add 25 μL/well of GMPPNP at varying concentrations to the BODIPY-FL-GDP loaded RhoA samples using a multichannel pipette.
Read the 384 plate 3 times immediately at 1-min intervals for 30 min.
Average and normalize the readings as a percentage of baseline fluorescence.
Plot the normalized data against time.
Process the data using GraphPad Prism.
Optional:
Prepare BODIPY-FL-GTPγS in buffer containing 20 mM Tris pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, and 10 mM EDTA.
Add RhoA samples to 96-well plate.
Read the 384-well plate with free BODIPY-FL-GTPγS 3 times using a plate reader.
Calculate the average baseline fluorescence from the readings.
Add 25 μL/well of the RhoA-GDP samples to the 384-well plate using a multichannel pipette.
Read the 384-well plate 3 times immediately at 1-min intervals for 30 min.
Calculate the average fluorescence from each set of readings.
Normalize the readings as a percentage of baseline fluorescence and plot against time.
Process the data using GraphPad Prism.
